title: Find the repeating and missing number
stepTitle: Solve Problems on Arrays [Easy -> Medium -> Hard]
category: Solve Problems on Arrays [Easy -> Medium -> Hard]
problemStatement: Array of 1..n where one value repeats and one is missing. Find both.
intuition: Two unknowns need two independent equations. Sum gives x - y; sum of squares gives x + y. Alternatively XOR everything and split by a differing bit — no overflow risk at all.

approaches.title: Better: frequency array
Optimal: sum and sum-of-squares
approaches.code:
def repeat_missing_math(a: list[int]) -> tuple[int, int]:
    n = len(a)
    sn = n * (n + 1) // 2
    s2n = n * (n + 1) * (2 * n + 1) // 6
    s = sum(a)
    s2 = sum(v * v for v in a)
    d = s - sn            # x - y
    t = (s2 - s2n) // d   # x + y
    x = (d + t) // 2
    return x, x - d
approaches.whyWorks: Two independent symmetric functions determine the unordered pair uniquely.

approaches.title: Optimal (overflow-safe): XOR bucket split
approaches.idea: XOR all values with 1..n, isolate a differing bit, split into two buckets.
approaches.whyWorks: x ^ y has a set bit wherever x and y differ; that bit partitions the multiset cleanly.

edgeCases: Overflow of sum-of-squares in C++/Java (use long long)
Deciding which bucket holds the repeater
commonMistakes: Integer overflow in the squares formula
Returning the pair in the wrong order
patternRecognition: Two unknowns -> two equations, or XOR bit-splitting
followUps: Solve with cyclic sort / index marking
Why is XOR preferred in Java?
interviewInsight: Offer the XOR method as the overflow-safe answer — it is what separates a good answer from a great one.
